acceptance_gates: Command bounding: 100% of issued actuator commands shall remain within configured min/max limits during validation runs.
Stale-data rejection: 100% of intentionally stale commands injected during test shall be rejected.
Timeout handling: 100% of simulated timeout events shall cause the controller to enter the defined fallback state.
Safe fallback: 100% of fallback transitions shall produce a documented safe actuator command or hold state.
Reference availability: A transparent reference path shall produce outputs for 100% of validation cases within the operating envelope.
Operating-envelope coverage: Validation shall include test cases spanning the full 20-55 m/s range.
Freshness enforcement: All accepted commands shall pass freshness checks with measured age below the configured freshness threshold.
Geometry handling: STL input shall be parsed successfully for all conformance test geometries in the approved dataset.
Interface integrity: All declared interfaces shall exchange data without schema or protocol errors in integration testing.
Traceability: Every control decision in validation shall be traceable to inputs, reference outputs, and safety-state outcomes.
constraints: Operating scope limited to the stated stream-velocity envelope.
Geometry input shall be accepted in STL format.
Reference geometry source shall be compatible with DrivAerML reference geometry.
Control outputs shall be bounded to prevent actuator overdrive.
Stale model commands shall be rejected.
Command timeout conditions shall trigger defined fallback behavior.
Safe fallback shall remain available independent of model output validity.
Any surrogate or controller evaluation shall be benchmarked against a transparent reference path.
No board, processor, or implementation fabric is implied by this contract.
No pretrained inference result is assumed.
No model accuracy is fabricated beyond measurable acceptance criteria.
All performance claims must be validated on the declared operating envelope.

child_handoff.rtl_spec_text:
Module adaptive_aero_control_top shall be a synthesizable FPGA-oriented RTL top level for active aerodynamic control supervision. The module shall not implement NVIDIA DoMINO inference, CFD, mesh processing, or tensor arithmetic. Instead, it shall provide a deterministic transport-and-safety wrapper around an external software or GPU service that performs the surrogate evaluation.

1. Clocking and reset:
- Inputs clk and rst_n shall clock and reset all internal state.
- Reset shall initialize the controller into safe fallback state, clear outstanding request state, clear fault latches, and set actuator command output to a configured safe default.

2. External register window:
- The module shall expose an implementation-friendly register window using reg_addr[7:0], reg_wdata[63:0], reg_rdata[63:0], reg_we, and reg_re.
- The register window shall be used to configure operating parameters including request enable, timeout limit, command clamp limits, fallback mode select, and sequence counters.
- The register window shall also expose status bits for busy, request_pending, response_valid, timeout_fault, stale_fault, malformed_response_fault, clamp_active, and fallback_active.
- The register file shall be small and synthesizable; it shall not contain bulk geometry storage or flow-field storage.

3. Model transport interface:
- The top level shall provide a bounded streaming request/response interface with no port wider than 128 bits.
- req_payload[127:0] shall carry a compact descriptor containing at minimum: request sequence ID, flow-condition encoding, geometry descriptor or host pointer token, operating-point identifier, and control flags.
- rsp_payload[127:0] shall carry a compact result packet containing at minimum: response sequence ID, validity flags, compact predicted aerodynamic metrics, and any service status code required by the host software.
- req_valid shall assert when a new request is available; req_ready shall qualify acceptance by the downstream transport.
- rsp_valid shall be sampled only when rsp_ready is asserted by the module.

4. Request handling:
- When enabled and not stalled, the module shall assemble a request packet from programmed configuration and issue it once per control cycle or on host command.
- The module shall track the outstanding request sequence ID and timestamp counter.
- The module shall prevent issuance of a new request that would overwrite an outstanding unacknowledged request unless a programmable overwrite mode explicitly allows it.

5. Response validation:
- The module shall verify that rsp_payload sequence ID matches the outstanding request.
- The module shall reject responses that are stale according to the configured timeout threshold, malformed according to protocol validity bits, or received when no request is pending.
- The module shall assert a fault when any response validation rule fails.
- The module shall only forward validated aerodynamic outputs into the command-selection path.

6. Safety and fallback:
- If no valid response arrives before timeout, the module shall enter fallback mode.
- Fallback mode shall drive a safe actuator command, which may be hold-last-good if explicitly configured and only if safety limits permit; otherwise it shall drive a neutral or minimum-drag safe default.
- The module shall clamp all actuator commands to programmable minimum and maximum bounds.
- The module shall provide fault signaling and status latch behavior until software clears the fault.

7. Actuator command generation:
- The module shall convert validated aerodynamic decisions into a compact actuator command bus of 32 bits or fewer.
- The command generator shall support a safe-default command, a validated model-driven command, and a fallback command.
- The command path shall include saturation logic and validity gating before asserting actuator_cmd_valid.

8. Storage and implementation constraints:
- For the FPGA prototype, payload storage shall use FPGA BRAM or host-managed memory access; no Sky130 hard macro shall be instantiated.
- The design shall not infer bulk payload memory using register arrays or generic SRAM modules in the FPGA top level.
- Only small control/status registers, counters, FSM state, and shadow copies of compact packet fields may be implemented in flip-flops.

9. Protocol and integration assumptions:
- The software side is responsible for packaging vehicle geometry from DrivAerML STL inputs and flow conditions into the compact request payload.
- The hardware side is responsible for transport, buffering of compact packets, validation, timeout enforcement, and actuator command safety.
- The architecture shall remain forward-compatible with future NVIDIA-hosted NIM or ChipLoop GPU worker execution using the same request/response contract.

10. Determinism and observability:
- The module shall provide sufficient status visibility for host software to reconstruct request issuance, response arrival, timeout events, stale-data rejection, and clamp activity.
- Any fault shall be observable through dedicated status bits and the fault output.
- The design shall be deterministic under identical request timing and register programming.

limitations: Surrogate inference and application-specific accuracy are not qualified in this run.
model_qualification.selection_basis: domain, interface, runtime, availability, and implementation-path compatibility

partition.decision: Partitioned for fpga_prototype as an FPGA-oriented transport-and-safety wrapper around an external CPU/GPU software surrogate service. The DoMINO surrogate remains in GPU/CPU software because the qualification run did not prove hardware-deployable inference. Hardware handles deterministic control supervision, validation, timeout handling, command clamping, and safe fallback; software handles STL geometry packaging, reference evaluation, surrogate execution, and optimization/validation analysis.
decision_factors: Selected model nvidia.domino.automotive_aero is provisionally compatible but not accuracy-qualified and explicitly requires a GPU worker/remote NIM runtime.
No evidence was provided that the surrogate is hardware-deployable, so it remains in GPU/CPU software.
The architecture specifies an FPGA-first control wrapper that does not implement the surrogate, only transport, validation, clamping, and fallback.
Acceptance gates require deterministic command bounding, stale-data rejection, timeout handling, and safe fallback, which are best enforced in FPGA logic.
Transparent reference computation is required for 100% of validation cases and is explicitly suited to CPU software for traceability.
STL geometry ingestion and DrivAerML-compatible packaging are software tasks due to parsing and host-memory handling needs.
Interface constraints favor compact register/packet protocols rather than large geometry tensors on hardware pins.
The implementation path is fpga_prototype, but the contract does not bind to a board or specific fabric.
Safety requirements mandate fault latching, safe default behavior, and independent fallback availability, which favors hardware enforcement of the last-mile control path.
Architecture optimization and validation traceability are design-time software activities rather than real-time hardware datapath functions.

jobs.latency_budget: offline or pre-cycle; must complete before control-cycle request issuance
jobs.rationale: Geometry parsing and STL handling are not hardware-deployable in the provided architecture and are better kept in software with direct access to host-managed memory and file I/O.
jobs.responsibility: Parse and validate STL geometry derived from DrivAerML reference geometry, perform structural readiness checks, and package a compact geometry descriptor or host pointer token for downstream use.

jobs.latency_budget: per evaluation/control cycle; sub-cycle on host side
jobs.rationale: Condition ingestion is a host/software concern because it is closely tied to orchestration, envelope validation, and request packaging.
jobs.responsibility: Receive, normalize, and range-check stream velocity inputs across 20-55 m/s and convert them into compact operating-point encodings for the control path.

jobs.latency_budget: validation-time / offline or nearline; must cover 100% of validation cases
jobs.rationale: The architecture explicitly assigns the transparent reference path to CPU software for traceability and validation. This path must remain observable and easy to audit.
jobs.responsibility: Compute the transparent baseline aerodynamic response/control estimate for every validation case and serve as the traceable reference path.

jobs.latency_budget: bounded by control timeout threshold configured in hardware; service must respond within the programmable timeout
jobs.rationale: The selected model requires a GPU worker and remote NIM-style runtime; no evidence supports hardware deployment, so it stays in GPU/CPU software.
jobs.responsibility: Execute the physics-based DoMINO surrogate in a remote GPU/CPU service using the compact request/response contract, without assuming RTL implementation.

jobs.latency_budget: per control cycle; must produce inputs before hardware commit deadline
jobs.rationale: High-level partitioning and policy assembly are best handled in software, while hardware enforces deterministic safety constraints.
jobs.responsibility: Separate estimation, decision logic, command shaping, validity checking, and safety supervision into explicit software responsibilities and generate compact control intent for hardware enforcement.

jobs.latency_budget: single control-cycle latency; deterministic and bounded
jobs.rationale: This is the core real-time safety function explicitly mapped to FPGA in the architecture, with small FSM, clamp logic, and command packing.
jobs.responsibility: Clamp actuator commands to configured min/max limits, gate updates on validity checks, and emit a compact actuator command bus only when all conditions pass.

jobs.latency_budget: hard real-time; must resolve within the configured timeout window and before command commit
jobs.rationale: The architecture and safety requirements assign freshness, stale-data, and timeout enforcement to deterministic hardware supervision.
jobs.responsibility: Track request sequence numbers, response age, elapsed timeout, and stale-data conditions; reject invalid or late model responses and assert faults as needed.

jobs.latency_budget: immediate on fault detection; no additional cycle beyond detection
jobs.rationale: Safe fallback must remain available independent of model validity, and the architecture explicitly places this in FPGA control supervision.
jobs.responsibility: Drive safe hold or predefined safe actuator state when model data is invalid, stale, missing, or timed out; maintain fault latching until cleared by software.

jobs.latency_budget: offline or nearline; must not delay control loop
jobs.rationale: Traceability and audit logging are richer software tasks and must support the documented acceptance gates and validation evidence.
jobs.responsibility: Record inputs, intermediate states, reference outputs, control outputs, faults, clamp events, stale rejections, and fallback transitions for acceptance-gate evidence.

jobs.rationale: Architecture definition and optimization are explicitly required and are best performed in software before or alongside hardware implementation.
jobs.responsibility: Explore and optimize system structure, interface sizing, timeout settings, fallback policies, and execution partitioning without binding to a specific board or fabric.

tradeoffs: Keeping the surrogate in GPU/CPU software preserves model flexibility and aligns with qualification status, but adds transport latency and service dependency.
Implementing command clamping, freshness checks, and fallback in FPGA improves determinism and safety, but constrains protocol complexity and limits on-device model logic.
Using a compact request/response interface simplifies hardware and I/O budget, but requires disciplined software packaging of geometry descriptors and control context.
CPU reference evaluation maximizes transparency and traceability, but may be slower than a specialized accelerator for large validation sweeps.
A hold-last-good fallback can improve drivability, but must be tightly bounded by safety rules to avoid propagating stale behavior.
Forward compatibility with future GPU/NIM execution is preserved, but the current design cannot claim hardware-surrogate acceleration benefits until the model is qualified for deployment.

architecture_decisions: Use an FPGA-first control architecture with a compact memory-mapped register interface rather than exposing geometry arrays or flow fields as top-level ports.
Keep the surrogate model outside RTL; RTL only handles transport, buffering, request tracking, validation, timeout management, and actuator command generation.
Adopt a CPU reference execution path for architecture-definition mode, with forward compatibility to future GPU/NIM execution through the same register protocol.
Limit top-level I/O to scalar control/status signals and a 64-bit-wide register window to remain implementation-friendly and below the 256 scalar-equivalent I/O target.
Represent vehicle geometry as a pointer/descriptor into host-managed memory or external software, not as RTL-managed bulk payload storage.
Implement stale-data rejection by sequence numbering, age limits, and response-validity checks before any actuator update is committed.
Implement command clamping in hardware against configured min/max actuator limits and a safe fallback state for any invalid, missing, or late model response.
Use a small FSM for request issuance, waiting, response capture, validation, and fallback arbitration.
Preserve a clean software/hardware split: software packages the DrivAerML STL geometry and flow conditions, while RTL manages deterministic control safety and timing.
For FPGA prototype, no Sky130 hard macro is used; payload buffering should rely on FPGA BRAM or host-side memory, with only small control registers in RTL.

architecture.product_summary: FPGA prototype for an intelligent active-aerodynamics controller operating from 20 to 55 m/s using a CPU reference path for DoMINO-based aerodynamics evaluation. The hardware does not implement the surrogate model itself; it provides a bounded request/response interface to software or GPU inference, validates inputs, detects stale or timed-out model responses, clamps actuator commands, and falls back to a safe aerodynamic mode when model data is invalid or unavailable.

safety_requirements: Reject any response that is stale, out of sequence, malformed, or inconsistent with the outstanding request ID.
Reject any command when the response age exceeds the programmable timeout threshold.
Clamp actuator outputs to programmable minimum and maximum limits before driving the actuator command bus.
Enter a safe fallback mode when the model path is unavailable, the request is not acknowledged, or the response is invalid.
Do not update actuator outputs from a response unless all validity checks pass.
Maintain a clear fault status until software explicitly acknowledges and clears the condition.
On reset, drive the actuator to a safe default and clear outstanding request tracking.
Do not rely on unbounded buffers, inferred payload FIFOs, or large register arrays for payload storage in the FPGA prototype.
verification_goals: Verify reset enters safe fallback state and clears all outstanding request tracking.
Verify register reads and writes correctly program timeout, clamp limits, enable bits, and fallback mode.
Verify request issuance uses the compact 128-bit payload and never exposes bulk geometry or flow fields on top-level pins.
Verify a valid response with matching sequence ID is accepted and propagates to actuator command generation.
Verify stale responses are rejected and raise the appropriate fault status.
Verify timeout expiration triggers fallback mode and safe actuator output.
Verify malformed or unexpected responses are rejected without updating actuator commands.
Verify actuator command clamping is enforced for both model-driven and fallback commands.
Verify no new request overwrites an outstanding request unless overwrite mode is explicitly enabled.
Verify fault latches remain asserted until software clears them.
Verify the design stays within the compact interface constraint and does not exceed the top-level I/O budget.
Verify FPGA implementation does not instantiate Sky130 macros and does not infer bulk payload storage in flip-flop arrays.
